release_notes: `DhanAdapter._note_rate_limit()`'s rolling rate-limit-hit counter was a per-process class attribute — since every strategy runs as its own OS subprocess, hits spread across concurrent subprocesses never accumulated anywhere. Despite sustained 429s recurring for days, the alert fired exactly once (2026-09-08). Now cross-process via a new `broker/_rate_gate.py::note_rate_limit()`, the same shared-SQLite pattern already used for pacing (`wait_turn()`) and the daily call counter (`record_call()`). `tests/test_dhan_adapter.py`'s isolation fixture mocked `wait_turn()` but not `record_call()`/`note_rate_limit()` — running that test file wrote real increments into the developer's actual dev `broker_rate_gate_dhan.sqlite`, inflating the real Settings-page "N calls today" counter with test noise. Now isolates `_rate_gate._DB_DIR` to a temp path, same as `tests/test_rate_gate.py` already does. `tests/test_broker.py::test_breeze_adapter_margins_returns_available_and_used` asserted the pre-0.37.16 subtraction formula for `BreezeAdapter.margins()` — that release correctly changed the code to add `block_by_trade_fno` back instead (live-confirmed against ICICI's own dashboard) and added its own new test elsewhere, but never updated this older pre-existing one, which had been quietly failing against the real, correct formula ever since. The code was right; only the test was stale.
